title: Correctness of the Two-Inequality Encoding for Modular Addition
summary: Experiments report correct division-property propagation for word sizes through seven, while proving the encoding correct for every word size remains unresolved.

formal_statement.body: $\forall n \ge 1$, prove that the two-inequality encoding yields the correct division-property propagation for addition modulo $2^n$.

scope.domain: The domain is division-property cryptanalysis of modular addition in symmetric ciphers.
parameters: n, the word size in bits
scope.unresolved_remainder: Prove correctness of the propagation encoding for arbitrary word sizes beyond the experimentally checked sizes up to seven.

citations.label: Alzette: a 64-bit ARX-box (feat. CRAX and TRAX)

progress.summary: The source reports that the two inequalities produce the correct division-property propagation table for word sizes up to seven in experiments, while noting a few redundant transitions. The open task is to establish the stated correctness for every word size.
citation_labels: Christof Beierle et al., Alzette: a 64-bit ARX-box (feat. CRAX and TRAX)
